message.content:
Below are three common ways to grab a screenshot of a webpage **using Python**. Pick the one that best fits your workflow: | Goal | Tool | Why it works | Quick‑start code | |------|------|--------------|------------------| | **Automated, headless capture** | **Selenium + ChromeDriver** | Selenium drives a real Chrome instance (or a headless one) and can capture the *visible* viewport or the *full page* via CDP. | ```python
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

# 1️⃣ Install ChromeDriver (matching your Chrome version).
# pip install chromedriver-autoinstaller
import chromedriver_autoinstaller
chromedriver_autoinstaller.install()

# 2️⃣ Configure Chrome (headless optional)
options = Options()
options.add_argument(\"--headless\") # remove if you want a visible window
options.add_argument(\"--disable-gpu\")\n# options.add_argument(\"--window-size=1920,1080\") # set size if needed\nservice = Service() # uses the auto‑installed driver\n\n# 3️⃣ Launch driver & navigate
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=options)\ndriver.get(\"https://www.example.com\")\n\n# 4️⃣ Screenshot – visible viewport\ndriver.save_screenshot(\"viewport.png\")\n\n# 5️⃣ Full‑page screenshot (via Chrome DevTools Protocol)\nfull_png = driver.execute_cdp_cmd(\"Page.captureScreenshot\", {\"format\": \"png\", \"captureBeyondViewport\": True})\nwith open(\"fullpage.png\", \"wb\") as f:\n f.write(base64.b64decode(full_png[\"data\"]))\n\ndriver.quit()\n``` | --- ### 1. Selenium + ChromeDriver (recommended) * **Pros** – Works on Windows, macOS, Linux; can run headless; can interact with the page before taking a shot. * **Cons** – Requires ChromeDriver binary that matches your Chrome version. #### Installation ```bash pip install selenium chromedriver-autoinstaller ``` #### Full‑page screenshot via CDP ```python full_png = driver.execute_cdp_cmd( "Page.captureScreenshot", {"format": "png", "captureBeyondViewport": True} ) image_bytes = base64.b64decode(full_png["data"]) with open("fullpage.png", "wb") as f: f.write(image_bytes) ``` --- ### 2. Playwright (modern alternative) Playwright is a newer library that supports Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. It has built‑in support for full‑page screenshots. ```bash pip install playwright playwright install # downloads browsers ``` ```python from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright with sync_playwright() as p: browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True) page = browser.new_page() page.goto("https://www.example.com") page.screenshot(path="screenshot.png", full_page=True) # full_page=True captures beyond viewport browser.close() ``` --- ### 3. OS‑level screenshot (no browser control) If you just want whatever is currently displayed on your screen (including a manually opened Chrome tab), you can use `pyautogui` or Pillow. ```bash pip install pyautogui pillow ``` ```python import pyautogui # Capture entire screen pyautogui.screenshot("screen.png") # Capture a region (x, y, width, height) region = (100, 200, 800, 600) # adjust to your Chrome window pyautogui.screenshot("region.png", region=region) ``` *Note:* This method does **not** know about the DOM; it simply grabs pixels from the display buffer. --- ## Which to choose? | Scenario | Best tool | |----------|-----------| | You need to automate navigation, click buttons, fill forms, then screenshot | Selenium or Playwright | | You want a quick “take whatever’s on the screen” snapshot | pyautogui / Pillow | | You need a headless, CI‑friendly solution | Playwright (simpler install) or Selenium with headless flag | --- ### Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **ChromeDriver mismatch** | Use `chromedriver-autoinstaller` or manually download the correct version. | | **Full‑page not captured** | In Selenium, use `execute_cdp_cmd("Page.captureScreenshot", {"captureBeyondViewport": True})`. | | **Headless mode hides UI elements** | Set `--window-size` to a realistic resolution so elements render correctly. | | **Permissions on macOS** | Grant “Screen Recording” permission to the terminal or IDE. | --- ### TL;DR ```python # Example: Selenium + ChromeDriver (full page) from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options import chromedriver_autoinstaller, base64 chromedriver_autoinstaller.install() options = Options(); options.add_argument("--headless") driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=Service(), options=options) driver.get("https://www.example.com") # Visible viewport driver.save_screenshot("viewport.png") # Full page full_png = driver.execute_cdp_cmd("Page.captureScreenshot", {"format":"png","captureBeyondViewport":True}) with open("fullpage.png","wb") as f: f.write(base64.b64decode(full_png["data"])) driver.quit() ``` That’s all you need to capture a screenshot of a website from Python!

from selenium import webdriver

If you want to capture the current tab that is already open, you can connect to existing Chrome instance via remote debugging port. Use `webdriver.Remote` with `desired_capabilities`. Or use `pychrome`.

Alternatively, use Playwright:

```
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=False)
    context = browser.new_context()
    page = context.new_page()
    page.goto("https://example.com")
    page.screenshot(path="screenshot.png", full_page=True)
```
